name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-16R 'Reclaim'
description:
The KPA-16R is not a new rifle. It is an officially sanctioned rebuild program — a KPA-16 platform that has been factory-returned, inspected, rebarreled with a new Slagworks chrome-lined 16-inch unit, refinished, and reissued with a new serial number and a 'Certified Reclaim' marking on the lower receiver. The upper receiver, handguard, and furniture may be original, refurbished, or replaced with new-production components depending on the inspection result; the internal components are individually assessed and replaced as needed. The trigger group is replaced as a unit regardless of condition. The resulting rifle is, by Kang-Petrov's published standards, functionally equivalent to a new KPA-16 — the 'Reclaim' designation carries a standard warranty and the same performance specifications as the new-production model.

The Reclaim program exists because GLMZ's Tier 1 market cannot always absorb the cost of new-production rifles, and Kang-Petrov and Slagworks Industrial recognized that a certified refurbishment pipeline was more profitable than leaving worn rifles to circulate in the gray market without quality oversight. The Reclaim program captures those rifles, certifies them, and returns them to commercial circulation at approximately 70% of new-production pricing. For Tier 1 buyers who are price-sensitive but want something with a warranty and traceable provenance, the Reclaim program is a genuine value proposition.

A KPA-16R with its Certified Reclaim marking carries complicated social meaning in GLMZ's armed communities. On the practical side, it's a functional rifle with a warranty at accessible pricing. On the social side, it marks its owner as someone who couldn't or wouldn't pay for new. Some shelf workers wear the Reclaim marking as a form of class solidarity — the rebuild rifle, the second-chance tool, the thing that keeps working after it should have been discarded. Others quietly sand off the Reclaim marking and carry the rifle without the designation visible. Both responses reveal something true about GLMZ's class dynamics.
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm Combat Standard
effective_range: 400m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.1 kg
tactical_use: Tactically identical to the new-production KPA-16. The Reclaim program's value is economic, not operational — a KPA-16R performs to the same specifications as a new KPA-16 and should be evaluated on those terms. Operators who receive Reclaim rifles in issued contexts sometimes spend additional time confirming function due to the rebuild nature of the platform, but a properly certified Reclaim rifle is not a liability.
cultural_context: The Reclaim program is Slagworks Industrial's most honest acknowledgment that the Tier 1 market exists and deserves product support. It's also a quality-control mechanism that captures rifles that would otherwise circulate in gray markets without inspection. The Certified Reclaim marking is simultaneously a warranty seal and a class marker, and GLMZ's armed communities read it differently depending on their own position in the social hierarchy. The marking can't be removed without voiding the warranty, which means every owner has to decide what to do with it.
known_users: community defense forces with limited budgets
shelf workers accessing rifles for the first time
story_hooks: A KPA-16R with a Certified Reclaim serial number is traced back through the rebuild program to an original serial that appears in Arcturus Civil Security's incident records from a significant engagement five years ago — the rifle was used in that engagement, recovered, turned over to Slagworks, and rebuilt. Someone who knows what that original serial means is now trying to buy back the rebuilt rifle specifically, which means they either have sentimental attachment to the weapon or need to recover something that was hidden inside the original lower receiver before it went into the rebuild program.

The Reclaim program's certification records have been accessed by an unauthorized party — not stolen, just read, which means someone was looking for information about specific rifles that passed through the rebuild program. The access was brief and targeted, and the serials looked up all trace back to the same original owner: a security contractor who died under unclear circumstances eighteen months ago.
